questions.stem: Nucleotides such as AMP, ADP, and ATP are the sensors of the energy status of the cell and their interconversion plays an important role in the energy homeostasis of the cell. Which of the following enzyme catalyzes the formation of AMP from two molecules of ADP?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adenylate kinase

When ATP level is reduced, AMP is formed by Adenylate kinase (ADK) in the following reaction:

  • Adenylate kinase or myokinase is a phosphotransferase (EC no-2)
  • It catalyzes the interconversion of adenine nucleotides (ATP, ADP, and AMP)
  • AMP is an allosteric activator of glycolysis.
  • Oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria is also dependent on the availability of ADP and is maintained by the action of adenylate kinase.
  • Some factors that modulate ADK activity and adenine nucleotide levels are Stress, exercise, hormone levels, and diet.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 109

questions.stem: Kinase enzymes most often catalyze the regulatory steps of cellular oxidative metabolic pathways. Which of the following activates Kinase of glycolysis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Insulin
  • Insulin activates all anabolic pathways/enzymes:
  • HMP
  • Glycogenesis
  • FA synthesis
  • Cholesterol synthesis
  • TG synthesis
  • Lipoprotein Lipase enzyme
  • But Insulin also activates two catabolic pathway enzymes, e. Glycolysis & Link reaction. It activates:
    • Glucokinase,
    • PFK-1, and
    • Pyruvate Kinase enzymes of glycolysis.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 184, Table 19.1

questions.stemHtml: A 28-year-old runner was advised to increase his carbohydrate intake after his daily training for ensuring enough muscle glycogen storage. The anabolic hormone released after such a meal will increase the activity of main muscle glycogenesis enzymes by:
questions.solutionHtml:
Activating phosphodiesterase
  • Insulin increases the activity of muscle glycogen synthase after the intake of carbohydrates lowering cellular cAMP levels through the activation of phosphodiesterase which converts cAMP to 5’ AMP. This results in the dephosphorylation of glycogen synthase causing its activation. (See fig. below)
  • Simultaneously, it also decreases the activity of glycogen phosphorylase thereby decreasing glycogenolysis.
  • Insulin does not affect the activity of adenylate cyclase. It is activated by glucagon.






Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No.145

questions.stem: Muscle glycogen is used for the rapid release of energy for performing intense physical exercise. Glycogenolysis is activated in muscles by the activity of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Epinephrine
  • Glycogenolysis is activated by both Glucagon and Epinephrine
  • As glucagon receptors are not found in muscle, So, only epinephrine increases glycogenolysis in muscle.
  • These hormones act by the action of mediator cAMP which causes phosphorylation of the enzyme of glycogen breakdown.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No.173

questions.stem: Cellular metabolism is greatly affected by hormones in response to changes in external conditions. which of the following effects on metabolism is/are exerted by the hormone cortisol?↑ Gluconeogenesis↑ Lipogenesis↑ Proteolysis↑ Export of amino acid to liver↑ GlycolysisSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1, 3, and 4 are correct
  • Cortisol is a catabolic hormone-like glucagon
  • It acts primarily on muscle, liver & adipose tissues.
  • A variety of stressors release cortisol from the adrenal cortex.
  • This is a relatively slow-acting hormone
  • It will cause an increase in the following:
    • Gluconeogenesis in the liver (by transport of amino acid substrates from peripheral tissues to the liver),
    • Proteolysis in peripheral tissues but induction of protein synthesis in the liver (by transport of amino acid from peripheral tissues to liver).




Textbook of Medical Biochemistry by Dinesh Puri 3rd Edition Page No. 625

questions.stem: Insulin and glucagon are major hormones affecting oxidative fuel metabolism. Which of the following enzyme will be activated with low Insulin: Glucagon ratio?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glucose -6-Phosphatase
  • Insulin is released in the Fed state.
  • Low Insulin: Glucagon ratio means ⇒ Catabolic state (As low insulin means Fasting state or catabolic state)
  • Insulin activates all anabolic enzymes with the exception that it also promotes catabolic pathways glycolysis and link reaction.
  • Glucose-6-Phosphatase is an enzyme that is active in the fasting state / catabolic state




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No.176

questions.stemHtml: Match the following:Select the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1-f, 2-e, 3-d, 4-b
  • Minor pathway for oxidation of glucose: HMP
  • The major pathway for oxidation of glucose: Glycolysis/ EMP
  • The pathway that occurs in fasting state/ Starvation: Gluconeogenesis
  • Amphibolic pathway (Both catabolic and anabolic pathway): TCA cycle
  • The pathway which occurs in both aerobic and anaerobic conditions: EMP/ Glycolysis



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 156, 163, 180, 191

questions.stem: Anabolic and catabolic processes in the body are generally activated in Fed and Fasting states respectively. The pathway which occurs both in Fed and Fasting state is:
questions.solutionHtml:
TCA
  • TCA and ETC are vital pathways that occur in both fed and fasting states.
  • TCA and ETC do not depend on hormones.
  • However, their activity can be either increased or decreased depending on the availability of substrates and the abundance of products respectively. For example: TCA activity is increased in the presence of oxaloacetate and acetyl CoA and decreased in the absence of NAD and FAD. Similarly, ETC activity can be decreased in the absence of oxygen.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 156

questions.stem: Phosphorylation and dephosphorylation of enzymes is one of the regulatory mechanisms for controlling their activity. Phosphorylation of which of the following enzymes will result in its activation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glycogen phosphorylase
  • Phosphorylation is done by the hormone glucagon. Glucagon is active in fasting or under catabolic situations. So, enzymes of the catabolic pathway (Except Glycolysis and Link reaction) will be active in the phosphorylated state
  • Glycogen phosphorylase is an enzyme helping in the breaking down of glycogen, it is a catabolic enzyme and all catabolic enzymes which are activated by glucagon are active in the phosphorylated state



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No.172

questions.stem: An injection of nitroglycerin given during an angiographic procedure acts by a secondary messenger which is formed from guanine-containing nucleotide as a precursor and causes vasodilation. This secondary messenger is also involved in which of the following process:
questions.solutionHtml:
ANP and BNP activation
  • Nucleotide GTP gives rise to secondary messenger cGMP by enzyme guanylate cyclase by cyclization.
  • cGMP - It consists of guanine, ribose, and phosphate
  • Hormones that use cGMP as a second messenger are called group IIb hormones. It has a role in the visual cycle, Vasodilatory effect by NO (nitric oxide), and activation of peptide hormones like ANP and BNP (atrial and brain natriuretic peptides).
  • The hormones which use cAMP as a second messenger are called group IIa hormones such as: Glucagon, LH, FSH, hCG, Calcitonin, Catecholamines



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No.331

questions.stem: Hormone insulin promotes a number of anabolic pathways and enzymes in the cell and body. The mechanism which is NOT responsible for promoting lipogenesis by insulin is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Inhibiting pyruvate dehydrogenase
  • Insulin Increases the formation of Acetyl CoA by increasing the action of enzyme – Pyruvate Dehydrogenase e. Link reaction
  • So, option C is wrong as insulin activates the enzyme of Link reaction i.e. Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (not inhibits).



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No.184

questions.stem: The nerve supply of 1st lumbrical is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Median Nerve

1st & 2nd lumbrical - supplied by median nerve, while 3rd & 4th lumbrical by the deep branch of ulnar nerve.





Gray’s Anatomy, 41st Edition, Page. No. 862

questions.stemHtml: Compression of the nerve within the carpal tunnel produces an inability to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Oppose the Thumb
  • The opposition of thumb - opponens pollicis - median nerve
  • In Carpal tunnel syndrome, the median nerve gets compressed under the flexor retinaculum, leading to paralysis of the muscles of the thenar eminence.
  • It is called an ‘ape-like or monkey-like hand’. There is loss of sensation in lateral 3½ digits including nail beds. The median nerve is the ‘eye of the hand’. There is little clawing of the index and middle fingers also.

Explanation for incorrect options: -

Option: A. Extend The Thumb

  • Extension of thumb - all extensor muscles - radial nerve

Option: B. Adduct the thumb

  • Adduction of thumb - adductor pollicis - ulnar nerve



Gray’s Anatomy, 41st Edition, Page. No. 862

questions.stemHtml: A 19-year male presents with complaints of hypoesthesia and wasting of the thenar eminence in his right hand. The nerve most likely to be affected in this case is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Median Nerve
  • Median nerve compression in the carpal tunnel at the wrist leads to Carpal Tunnel syndrome.
  • This syndrome consists of motor, sensory, vasomotor, and trophic symptoms in the hand caused by compression of the median nerve in the carpal tunnel.
  • Examination reveals wasting of thenar eminence (ape-like hand), and hypoesthesia to light touch on the palmar aspect of lateral 3½ digits.
  • However, the skin over the thenar eminence is not affected as the branch of the median nerve supplying it arises in the forearm. 

Symptoms and signs

Findings indicative of CTS

Age

40-60 years

Gender

Female > males

Risk Factors

Obesity, Diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism, rheumatoid arthritis, Chronic Renal failure, pregnancy

Occupation

More in occupation involving repeated hand

movements or vibrations

Sensory symptoms

Pain

Paresthesia

Numbness

Classic or Probable pattern of Katz Hand Diagram

Flicks sign

Motor symptoms

Hand Clumsiness

Weakness of Thumb

 Atrophy of Thenar Muscles

Autonomic symptoms

Swelling or Feeling of Tightness in Hand

Temperature change

Difference in skin color

Difference in sympathetic skin response of median to ulnar nerve

Provocative tests

Phalen's test

Tinel sign

Manual Carpal Compression test



Gray’s Anatomy, 41st Edition, Page. No. 862

questions.stemHtml: Select the most appropriate statement regarding the Median nerve:

options.label: A
options.text: Arises from the posterior and medial cords of the brachial plexus

options.label: B
options.text: Passes from the medial to the lateral; side of the brachial artery in the arm

options.label: C
options.text: Gives no muscular branches in the arm

options.label: D
options.text: Enters the forearm muscles by passing between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris

questions.answerText: Gives no muscular branches in the arm
questions.solutionHtml:
Gives no muscular branches in the arm
  • The only branch the median nerve gives in the arm is a branch to the elbow joint.



Gray’s Anatomy, 41st Edition, Page. No. 862

questions.stemHtml: A young boy who was driving a motorcycle at high speed collided with a tree and was thrown on his right shoulder. Though there was no fracture, his right arm was medially rotated and his forearm pronated. The following facts concerning this patient are correct, except:

options.label: A
options.text: The injury was at Erb’s point

options.label: B
options.text: A lesion of C-5 and C-6 was present

options.label: C
options.text: The median and ulnar nerve was affected

options.label: D
options.text: Supraspinatus and infraspinatus, subclavius, and biceps brachii were paralyzed

questions.answerText: The median and ulnar nerve was affected
questions.solutionHtml:
The median and ulnar nerve was affected
  • If the Median and Ulnar nerves are both affected, then the boy must present with features of a complete claw hand along with paralysis of all flexor muscles of the foramen and intrinsic muscles of the hand.



Gray’s Anatomy, 41st Edition, Page. No. 862
